# About

**Happy Horse 1.0** uses the model ID `alibaba/happy-horse/image-to-video`. Happy Horse 1.0 - Image to Video. Configured Alibaba route; cloned from hh/image-to-video.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/alibaba/happy-horse/image-to-video` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Setup

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | `integer` | No | `—` | Minimum: 1. Maximum: 2147483646. |
| `prompt` | `string` | No | `—` | Prompt. |
| `duration` | `integer` | No | `5` | Duration. Minimum: 2. Maximum: 15. |
| `image_url` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Image URL. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"720p"` | Options: 720p, 1080p. |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns the generated file in the `video` field.

### Submit and wait

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "alibaba/happy-horse/image-to-video",
  {
    input: {
      "duration": 5,
      "image_url": "https://example.com/input.jpg",
      "resolution": "720p"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    'alibaba/happy-horse/image-to-video',
    arguments={'duration': 5,
         'image_url': 'https://example.com/input.jpg',
         'resolution': '720p'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/alibaba/happy-horse/image-to-video' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "duration": 5,
  "image_url": "https://example.com/input.jpg",
  "resolution": "720p"
}
JSON
```

### Explicit lifecycle control

Use the Python SDK when a worker needs explicit status, result, or cancellation control for an existing request. The TypeScript v2 client currently exposes automatic polling through `subscribe`.

```python
import higgsfield_client

request_id = "{request_id}"
status = higgsfield_client.status(request_id=request_id)
result = higgsfield_client.result(request_id=request_id)
higgsfield_client.cancel(request_id=request_id)
```

seed.description: Optional random seed for similar, reproducible results.

prompt.description: Positive prompt or editing instruction in Chinese or English. Alibaba recommends at most 4,500 tokens.

image_urls.description: One to three ordered public image URLs used as editing references.

resolution.description: Output resolution tier. Both tiers produce PNG images.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio. Exact provider-recommended dimensions are selected automatically.

prompt_extend.description: Improve the prompt before generation. Required when thinking mode is enabled.

enable_thinking.description: Use model reasoning to improve image quality. Requires prompt enhancement.

negative_prompt.description: Content, styles, or artifacts to avoid in the output.

prompt_extend_mode.description: Direct enhancement is available for every request; agent enhancement is text-to-image only.

## 3. Queue

## 4. Draft previews and finalization

Create a preview, review it, and finalize the selected draft at 1080p using `bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft`.

### 1. Create a draft

Send the usual inputs for your generation endpoint with `draft: true`. Omitting `draft` or setting it to `false` keeps regular generation behavior. Draft mode forces **480p, MP4, and standard bitrate**, even if the request selects another supported resolution, format, or bitrate.

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "image_url": "https://example.com/input.jpg",
  "prompt": "The camera slowly moves closer",
  "duration": 5,
  "draft": true
}
JSON
```

Replace example media URLs with your own accessible media URLs. Save the `request_id` from the POST response. This is the public request ID (JobSet ID) that you will pass as `draft_id`; do not use a video URL, an internal job ID, or a provider task ID.

### 2. Wait for the draft and review it

Poll the returned `status_url` with the same authorization header, or use the status endpoint directly:

```bash
DRAFT_REQUEST_ID="REPLACE_WITH_DRAFT_REQUEST_ID"
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${DRAFT_REQUEST_ID}/status" \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY"
```

Wait until `status` is `completed`, then review the preview at `video.url` in the status response. Do not finalize a request that is queued, in progress, failed, canceled, or blocked by moderation.

### 3. Finalize at 1080p

Submit a new request to `bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft`. Replace the example UUID below with the draft's saved `request_id`:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "draft_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "resolution": "1080p"
}
JSON
```

The response contains a **new** `request_id` and `status_url` for finalization. Poll that new status URL until `status` is `completed`; its `video.url` is the final video. Keep the draft and finalization request IDs separate.

### Pricing

Draft generation and finalization are separate paid requests. Each is billed per **output second** at its own resolution. Finalization uses the duration and video-input pricing tier saved with the draft and applies the 1080p rate; it does not reuse the draft's charge. The draft charge is not deducted from the finalization charge.

| Input type | 480p draft, USD / output second | 1080p finalization, USD / output second |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without video input (text, images, or audio only) | $0.1177 | $0.6518 |
| With video input | $0.1387 | $0.7858 |

These are standard self-serve rates. Total cost for a draft followed by one finalization is `output seconds × (draft rate + finalization rate)`. If you stop after viewing the draft, only the draft request is charged. Input-video seconds are not added to the billing multiplier. For video edit, output duration is derived from the primary input video; for video extend, the billed duration is the requested extension.

### Requirements and limits

- Use a completed draft created with `draft: true` on one of the five `bytedance/seedance-2.5/` generation endpoints listed below. A regular generation cannot be finalized as a draft.
- The draft must belong to the same account as the finalization request and contain a single video job.
- Finalize within seven days of draft creation and before the request's retention expires. A shorter account retention or `Hf-Expires-After` setting can shorten this window. If the status response includes `expires_at`, respect that timestamp as well as the seven-day limit. Deleted or purged drafts cannot be finalized.
- Only `1080p` is supported for finalization. It is also the default when `resolution` is omitted.
- Finalization accepts `draft_id` and `resolution`. Prompt, media inputs, audio settings, aspect ratio, and duration come from the original draft. To change those inputs, create a new draft.
- Draft creation and finalization use TTUS. You do not need to select a provider or send a provider task ID.

### Supported draft endpoints

- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-extend`

# About

**Seedance 2.5** uses the model ID `bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit`. Seedance 2.5 Video Edit enables video-to-video transformation by editing existing videos with prompts and optional audio, image, or additional video inputs. It supports output customization including resolution and format, with optional audio generation.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Setup

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Minimum length: 1. |
| `video_url` | `string` | Yes | `—` |  |
| `audio_urls` | `array[string]` | No | `—` |  |
| `image_urls` | `array[string]` | No | `—` |  |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"720p"` | Options: 480p, 720p, 1080p. |
| `video_urls` | `array[string]` | No | `—` |  |
| `output_format` | `string` | No | `"mp4"` | Options: mp4, mov. |
| `generate_audio` | `boolean` | No | `true` |  |
| `draft` | `boolean` | No | `false` | Create a 480p MP4 preview with standard bitrate for later 1080p finalization. See the draft workflow below. |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns the generated file in the `video` field.

### Submit and wait

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit",
  {
    input: {
      "prompt": "A cinematic scene at sunset",
      "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
      "resolution": "720p",
      "output_format": "mp4",
      "generate_audio": true
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    'bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit',
    arguments={'prompt': 'A cinematic scene at sunset',
         'video_url': 'https://example.com/input.mp4',
         'resolution': '720p',
         'output_format': 'mp4',
         'generate_audio': True},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "A cinematic scene at sunset",
  "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
  "resolution": "720p",
  "output_format": "mp4",
  "generate_audio": true
}
JSON
```

### Explicit lifecycle control

Use the Python SDK when a worker needs explicit status, result, or cancellation control for an existing request. The TypeScript v2 client currently exposes automatic polling through `subscribe`.

```python
import higgsfield_client

request_id = "{request_id}"
status = higgsfield_client.status(request_id=request_id)
result = higgsfield_client.result(request_id=request_id)
higgsfield_client.cancel(request_id=request_id)
```

## 4. Draft previews and finalization

Create a preview, review it, and finalize the selected draft at 1080p using `bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft`.

### 1. Create a draft

Send the usual inputs for your generation endpoint with `draft: true`. Omitting `draft` or setting it to `false` keeps regular generation behavior. Draft mode forces **480p, MP4, and standard bitrate**, even if the request selects another supported resolution, format, or bitrate.

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "Change the scene to a snowy landscape",
  "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
  "draft": true
}
JSON
```

Replace example media URLs with your own accessible media URLs. Save the `request_id` from the POST response. This is the public request ID (JobSet ID) that you will pass as `draft_id`; do not use a video URL, an internal job ID, or a provider task ID.

### 2. Wait for the draft and review it

Poll the returned `status_url` with the same authorization header, or use the status endpoint directly:

```bash
DRAFT_REQUEST_ID="REPLACE_WITH_DRAFT_REQUEST_ID"
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/${DRAFT_REQUEST_ID}/status" \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY"
```

Wait until `status` is `completed`, then review the preview at `video.url` in the status response. Do not finalize a request that is queued, in progress, failed, canceled, or blocked by moderation.

### 3. Finalize at 1080p

Submit a new request to `bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft`. Replace the example UUID below with the draft's saved `request_id`:

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/finalize-draft' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "draft_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
  "resolution": "1080p"
}
JSON
```

The response contains a **new** `request_id` and `status_url` for finalization. Poll that new status URL until `status` is `completed`; its `video.url` is the final video. Keep the draft and finalization request IDs separate.

### Pricing

Draft generation and finalization are separate paid requests. Each is billed per **output second** at its own resolution. Finalization uses the duration and video-input pricing tier saved with the draft and applies the 1080p rate; it does not reuse the draft's charge. The draft charge is not deducted from the finalization charge.

| Input type | 480p draft, USD / output second | 1080p finalization, USD / output second |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Without video input (text, images, or audio only) | $0.1177 | $0.6518 |
| With video input | $0.1387 | $0.7858 |

These are standard self-serve rates. Total cost for a draft followed by one finalization is `output seconds × (draft rate + finalization rate)`. If you stop after viewing the draft, only the draft request is charged. Input-video seconds are not added to the billing multiplier. For video edit, output duration is derived from the primary input video; for video extend, the billed duration is the requested extension.

### Requirements and limits

- Use a completed draft created with `draft: true` on one of the five `bytedance/seedance-2.5/` generation endpoints listed below. A regular generation cannot be finalized as a draft.
- The draft must belong to the same account as the finalization request and contain a single video job.
- Finalize within seven days of draft creation and before the request's retention expires. A shorter account retention or `Hf-Expires-After` setting can shorten this window. If the status response includes `expires_at`, respect that timestamp as well as the seven-day limit. Deleted or purged drafts cannot be finalized.
- Only `1080p` is supported for finalization. It is also the default when `resolution` is omitted.
- Finalization accepts `draft_id` and `resolution`. Prompt, media inputs, audio settings, aspect ratio, and duration come from the original draft. To change those inputs, create a new draft.
- Draft creation and finalization use TTUS. You do not need to select a provider or send a provider task ID.

### Supported draft endpoints

- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-edit`
- `bytedance/seedance-2.5/video-extend`

# About

**Seedream 5.0 Pro** uses the model ID `bytedance/seedream/v5.0/pro/edit`. Edit and combine images with Seedream 5.0 Pro using a prompt and up to 10 reference images. Change subjects, colors or composition and generate one result at 1K, 1.5K or 2K.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.0/pro/edit` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Setup

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Prompt. Minimum length: 1. |
| `image_urls` | `array[string]` | Yes | `—` | Image URLs. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"2k"` | Resolution. Options: 1k, 1.5k, 2k. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `string` | No | `"1:1"` | Aspect Ratio. Options: auto, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9, 3:2, 21:9, 3:4, 9:16, 2:3. |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns generated files in the `images` array.

### Submit and wait

Replace placeholder media URLs with accessible URLs for your own files.

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
  baseURL: "https://api.higgsfield.ai",
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "bytedance/seedream/v5.0/pro/edit",
  {
    input: {
      "prompt": "Change the bottle in the reference image to emerald green, keeping the lighting and composition",
      "image_urls": [
        "https://example.com/reference.png"
      ],
      "resolution": "2k",
      "aspect_ratio": "1:1"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
from higgsfield_client import SyncClient

client = SyncClient(base_url="https://api.higgsfield.ai")
result = client.subscribe(
    'bytedance/seedream/v5.0/pro/edit',
    arguments={'prompt': 'Change the bottle in the reference image to emerald green, '
                   'keeping the lighting and composition',
         'image_urls': ['https://example.com/reference.png'],
         'resolution': '2k',
         'aspect_ratio': '1:1'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/bytedance/seedream/v5.0/pro/edit' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "Change the bottle in the reference image to emerald green, keeping the lighting and composition",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://example.com/reference.png"
  ],
  "resolution": "2k",
  "aspect_ratio": "1:1"
}
JSON
```

### Custom polling

For direct HTTP integration, submit the request and poll the returned `status_url` using the same API credentials until it reaches a terminal status. Use the returned `cancel_url` to request cancellation while the request is still queued. See the [request lifecycle guide](https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/requests.md) for response states.

## 4. Using this model

Provide a non-empty `prompt` and 1–10 URLs in `image_urls`. Describe the intended edits and how each reference should be used. Choose `resolution` from `1k`, `1.5k` or `2k` (default `2k`); `aspect_ratio` defaults to `1:1`. This endpoint produces one image and does not expose layer separation.

## 5. Pricing

| Resolution | Price per image |
| --- | --- |
| `1k` | $0.054 |
| `1.5k` | $0.054 |
| `2k` | $0.108 |

Each request generates one image. Reference images do not add a separate charge. The default `2k` request costs $0.108.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/image-to-image` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

## 4. Custom references (Soul ID)

A [Soul ID](https://open.higgsfield.ai/models/soul-id/playground) is a trained custom reference that lets you reuse a person's identity in Soul 2 generations. Create it once, wait for training to finish, and pass its ID as `custom_reference_id`.

### Create a Soul ID for Soul 2

Send `POST /v1/custom-references` with a name, 1–100 input images, and **`model_version: "v2"`**. The default model version is `v1`, so explicitly select `v2` for Soul 2. Replace the example URLs with accessible images of the person you want to use.

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/v1/custom-references' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "My Soul 2 character",
  "model_version": "v2",
  "input_images": [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": "https://example.com/portrait-1.jpg"},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": "https://example.com/portrait-2.jpg"}
  ]
}
JSON
```

Save the response's `id`. This is the Soul ID to use as `custom_reference_id`; it is not a generation `request_id`.

### Wait until the reference is ready

```bash
REFERENCE_ID="YOUR_SOUL_ID"
curl --request GET \
  --url "https://api.higgsfield.ai/v1/custom-references/${REFERENCE_ID}" \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY"
```

Repeat the GET request at intervals until `status` is `completed`. If it is `failed`, training did not produce a usable reference. You can find existing Soul IDs with `GET /v1/custom-references/list?page=1&page_size=20`.

Use credentials belonging to the same API account for creation and generation. References belonging to another account, missing references, and references whose status is not `completed` cannot be used.

### Generate with your Soul ID

Replace `YOUR_COMPLETED_SOUL_ID` with the UUID returned when creating the reference. `custom_reference_strength` is optional, defaults to `1.0`, and accepts values from `0` to `1`.

For image-to-image, also provide `image_url`: it supplies the scene reference, while `custom_reference_id` supplies the trained character identity. Reference-image prompt processing remains enabled.

```bash
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield-ai/soul/v2/image-to-image' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "image_url": "https://example.com/reference.jpg",
  "prompt": "A natural portrait of this person in soft window light",
  "custom_reference_id": "YOUR_COMPLETED_SOUL_ID",
  "custom_reference_strength": 1.0,
  "enhance_prompt": true,
  "resolution": "720p",
  "aspect_ratio": "1:1",
  "batch_size": 1
}
JSON
```

The generation response contains `request_id` and `status_url`. Poll `status_url` until completion and read the generated image URLs from `images`.

# AI Influencer

Create a character reference sheet with a close-up portrait and a full-body view. Choose a human or animal character, customize its appearance, and optionally supply an identity photo and clothing or item references.

Each request produces **one 2K image at 16:9**, with Medium quality. The price is **$0.05 per sheet** for every character type, before any account-specific discounts. Resolution, aspect ratio and quality are fixed.

## Quick start

Send a JSON request to `POST https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/ai-influencer` with your API key:

```bash
curl --request POST 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/ai-influencer' \
  --header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY}" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"tier":"normal","selection":{"gender":["female"],"body_type":["body_athletic"],"height":["h_tall"]},"seed":42817}'
```

Set `HF_API_KEY` to your `key-id:secret`. All input fields are optional; the default character type is `normal`.

Generation is asynchronous. The response includes `request_id`, `status`, `status_url` and `cancel_url`. Poll the returned `status_url` with the same authorization header. When `status` is `completed`, the generated sheet is available at `images[0].url`.

## Character types

| `tier` | Playground label | Character |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `normal` | Average | Human with natural appearance; default |
| `freak` | Bold | Human with more unusual appearance traits |
| `total` | Extreme | Human with stronger appearance transformations |
| `insects` | Insect | Insect character |
| `frogs` | Frog | Frog character |
| `cats` | Cat | Cat character |
| `dogs` | Dog | Dog character |
| `capybaras` | Rodent | Capybara character |
| `birds` | Bird | Bird character |

Use the API values in the first column, not the display labels.

## Inputs

| Parameter | Type / default | Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tier` | string, `"normal"` | One of the nine character types above. |
| `selection` | object, `{}` | Category keys mapped to arrays of option keys. Up to 18 categories; each category has its own selection limit. Discover current keys through the options endpoint below. |
| `image_url` | URL or null, `null` | One identity reference photo. This is separate from item references. |
| `item_image_urls` | URL array, `[]` | Up to three clothing, footwear or item references, in order. |
| `brief` | string, `""` | Optional character direction, up to 4,000 characters. Supported by the API even though hidden in the playground form. |
| `seed` | integer or null, `null` | Character-selection seed from 1 to 1,000,000. Omit it for an automatically generated seed. |
| `variation_index` | integer, `0` | Animal sequence position from 0 to 2,147,483,647. Human types require `0`. |
| `body_color` | string or null | Optional animal body color as `#RRGGBB`. Human types require omission or null. |
| `pinned_species` | string or null | Optional valid insect species ID, 1–64 characters, to keep the species fixed while varying its look. Only supported with `tier="insects"`. Unknown IDs are rejected. |
| `trait_variants` | object or null, `null` | Advanced overrides for selected appearance traits; normally omit this field. See below. |

Image URLs must be reachable by the API and point to non-animated JPEG, PNG or WebP files. The download limit is 64 MiB per image; images must also pass decoding and image validation. Upload local files first and pass their URLs, rather than file objects or base64 data.

### Identity photo and item references

`image_url` is the **Upload your photo** field. `item_image_urls` is **Add elements or references**. The identity photo does not count toward the three-item limit.

```json
{
  "tier": "normal",
  "image_url": "https://example.com/identity.jpg",
  "item_image_urls": [
    "https://example.com/jacket.png",
    "https://example.com/shoes.png"
  ],
  "seed": 42817
}
```

Replace these example URLs with your uploaded images. The identity reference guides the character's likeness; item references guide clothing or other items.

## Appearance options

Fetch `GET https://api.higgsfield.ai/models/higgsfield/ai-influencer/options` to discover the current catalog. This endpoint does not require authentication when the model is visible and publicly available; it returns `404` while the model is hidden or unavailable in the public catalog. Generation always requires authentication and model access.

The response contains `config_revision` and `categories`. Each category provides `key`, `label`, `tiers`, `max` and `options`. Each option provides `key`, `label`, nullable `img`, nullable `color`, nullable `tiers`, nullable `slot` and `exclusive`.

To build a selection:

1. Keep categories whose `tiers` include the selected character type. Human and animal categories can share a key; choose the matching tier's category.
2. If an option has a non-null `tiers` list, show it only for those types.
3. Send category and option **keys** in `selection`, with at most `max` options per category. Select at most one option for each non-null facial `slot`. An `exclusive` option must be selected alone in its category.
4. Use `img` for previews, `color` for color swatches, and labels when no visual is provided. A null preview does not mean the option is invalid. Preserve catalog order and refresh cached choices when `config_revision` changes.

For example:

```json
{
  "tier": "normal",
  "selection": {
    "gender": ["female"],
    "body_type": ["body_athletic"],
    "height": ["h_tall"]
  }
}
```

The catalog includes human settings such as gender, ethnicity, age, skin tone, height, body type, proportions, eyes, hair, distinctive features, style and accessories. Available options depend on the character type. Rebuild or filter selections when switching between human and animal types; stale or incompatible keys are rejected.

## Animal variations

Keep `seed` and `tier` fixed and increment `variation_index` for successive animal selections:

```json
{
  "tier": "cats",
  "seed": 42817,
  "variation_index": 0,
  "body_color": "#D9A066"
}
```

Use index `1` for the next request, then `2`, and so on. Species cycle through the available set without repeats within a cycle, while appearance components vary independently. Explicit selections and trait overrides can constrain the variation; pinning an insect species keeps that species fixed.

The seed controls character selection, not exact output pixels. Repeating a seed and index does not guarantee an identical rendered image, and catalog changes can affect future selections. An automatically generated seed is not returned as additional response metadata; supply and store your own seed when you need a sequence. Use the standard `Idempotency-Key` header to deduplicate retries, with a new key for each new variation.

## Advanced trait overrides

When supplying `trait_variants`, include `"version": "appearance-v2"` and a `choices` object mapping eligible selected trait keys to their supported variant IDs. General variants are `original` and `v1`–`v5`; the current schema additionally permits `v1`–`v10` for `pr_centaur`. Variants must be supported by the current trait catalog.

For animals, optional `animal_choices` maps eligible selected animal option keys to integer indices `0`–`4`. This field must be omitted or null for human types. Unspecified eligible traits use their original/default variant when an override object is supplied. The public options endpoint does not expose the internal trait-variant or insect-species catalogs; omit these advanced overrides unless you already have valid identifiers.

# About

**Genjutsu Motion Transfer** uses the model ID `higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0`. The source video must be at least 4 seconds. Videos longer than 30 seconds are trimmed to 30 seconds; output duration follows the prepared source video. Provide 1–8 image references. The prompt is optional and defaults to an empty string.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Setup

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | No | `""` | Prompt. Maximum length: 10000. |
| `video_url` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Video Url. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 2083. |
| `image_urls` | `array[string]` | Yes | `—` | Image Urls. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"720p"` | Resolution. Options: 720p, 480p, 1080p. |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns the generated file in the `video` field.

### Submit and wait

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0",
  {
    input: {
      "prompt": "",
      "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
      "image_urls": [
        "https://example.com/input.jpg"
      ],
      "resolution": "720p"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    'higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0',
    arguments={'prompt': '',
         'video_url': 'https://example.com/input.mp4',
         'image_urls': ['https://example.com/input.jpg'],
         'resolution': '720p'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/higgsfield/genjutsu/motion-transfer/v1.0' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "",
  "video_url": "https://example.com/input.mp4",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://example.com/input.jpg"
  ],
  "resolution": "720p"
}
JSON
```

### Explicit lifecycle control

Use the Python SDK when a worker needs explicit status, result, or cancellation control for an existing request. The TypeScript v2 client currently exposes automatic polling through `subscribe`.

```python
import higgsfield_client

request_id = "{request_id}"
status = higgsfield_client.status(request_id=request_id)
result = higgsfield_client.result(request_id=request_id)
higgsfield_client.cancel(request_id=request_id)
```

# About

**Kling Image 4.0** uses the model ID `kling-image/v4.0/edit`. Edit images with Kling Image 4.0 using a prompt and up to 10 references. Adjust composition, subjects or visual style and generate one image at 2K, 4K or native 8K.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/kling-image/v4.0/edit` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript

```



### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Prompt. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 50000. |
| `image_urls` | `array[string]` | Yes | `—` | JPG/PNG, up to 30 MB, dimensions at least 300 px and aspect ratio 2:5 to 5:2. Reference as @image_1, @image_2, etc. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"2k"` | Options: 2k, 4k, 8k. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `string` | No | `"auto"` | Options: 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:3, 3:4, 3:2, 2:3, 21:9, auto. |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns generated files in the `images` array.

### Submit and wait

Replace placeholder media URLs with accessible URLs for your own files.

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
  baseURL: "https://api.higgsfield.ai",
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "kling-image/v4.0/edit",
  {
    input: {
      "prompt": "Place the product from @image_1 on pale stone, keeping its shape and label",
      "image_urls": [
        "https://example.com/reference.png"
      ],
      "resolution": "2k",
      "aspect_ratio": "16:9"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
from higgsfield_client import SyncClient

client = SyncClient(base_url="https://api.higgsfield.ai")
result = client.subscribe(
    'kling-image/v4.0/edit',
    arguments={'prompt': 'Place the product from @image_1 on pale stone, keeping its shape '
                   'and label',
         'image_urls': ['https://example.com/reference.png'],
         'resolution': '2k',
         'aspect_ratio': '16:9'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/kling-image/v4.0/edit' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "Place the product from @image_1 on pale stone, keeping its shape and label",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://example.com/reference.png"
  ],
  "resolution": "2k",
  "aspect_ratio": "16:9"
}
JSON
```

### Custom polling

For direct HTTP integration, submit the request and poll the returned `status_url` using the same API credentials until it reaches a terminal status. Use the returned `cancel_url` to request cancellation while the request is still queued. See the [request lifecycle guide](https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/requests.md) for response states.

## 4. Using this model

Use a non-empty `prompt` of at most 50,000 characters. `resolution` accepts `2k`, `4k` or `8k` and defaults to `2k`. `aspect_ratio` defaults to `auto`; supported values are listed above.

Supply 1–10 JPG or PNG URLs in `image_urls`. Each image must be at most 30 MB, at least 300 pixels on each side, with an aspect ratio between 2:5 and 5:2. Refer to images in the prompt as `@image_1`, `@image_2`, and so on.

This endpoint generates one image. Use the separate Series variant for 2–10 related images; this endpoint has no series-count parameter.

## 5. Pricing

| Resolution | Price per image |
| --- | --- |
| `2k` | $0.063 |
| `4k` | $0.094 |
| `8k` | $0.157 |

Each request generates one image. A default 2K request costs $0.063. Reference images do not add a separate charge.

# Kling 4.0 — Image to Video

Animate a required first frame, optionally guiding the sequence with middle frames and an end frame. Generate a 3–30 second video in 720p or 1080p.

**Model ID:** `kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video`

## 1. Calling the API

Send a JSON POST request to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video`. Authenticate with `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET`.

### SDK setup

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

Keep API credentials on your server and out of browser code and source control.

## 2. Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_url` | `string` | Yes | — | First frame. A non-empty image URL is always required. |
| `prompt` | `string` | No | — | Describe the desired action, transitions, and camera movement. May be omitted. |
| `image_urls` | `string[]` | No | — | Middle frames, in sequence order. Maximum 8 images, even when the end frame is omitted. These are intermediate keyframes, not general reference images. |
| `end_image_url` | `string` | No | — | Optional end frame. Does not replace the required first frame. |
| `duration` | `integer` | No | 10 | Output duration in seconds. Integer from 3 to 30. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | 1080p | Output resolution: `720p` or `1080p`. |

Defaults apply when a field is omitted. Send media as non-empty URLs accessible to the service, not local file paths. Replace the `example.com` URLs in the examples with your own reachable media URLs.

## 3. Using this model

### Frame order

Frames are sent in this order: `image_url` → each entry in `image_urls` → `end_image_url`, if supplied. Put middle frames in the order you want them used. The schema allows at most 8 middle frames, leaving room for one first frame and one end frame: up to 10 images in total.

Only `image_url` is required. An end frame or middle frames alone cannot start a valid request. Omit unused optional frame fields rather than sending empty URL strings.

### Output framing

This endpoint does not expose an `aspect_ratio` parameter. Prepare your input frames with the desired composition; use `resolution` to select 720p or 1080p output.

## 4. Request examples

### Submit and wait

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video",
  {
    input: {
      "image_url": "https://example.com/first-frame.jpg",
      "prompt": "The camera slowly moves forward as the subject turns toward the sunlight.",
      "duration": 10,
      "resolution": "1080p"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    'kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video',
    arguments={'image_url': 'https://example.com/first-frame.jpg',
         'prompt': 'The camera slowly moves forward as the subject turns toward the '
                   'sunlight.',
         'duration': 10,
         'resolution': '1080p'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/kling-video/v4.0/image-to-video' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "image_url": "https://example.com/first-frame.jpg",
  "prompt": "The camera slowly moves forward as the subject turns toward the sunlight.",
  "duration": 10,
  "resolution": "1080p"
}
JSON
```

### First, middle, and end frames

Use this JSON body with the same model endpoint:

```json
{
  "image_url": "https://example.com/first-frame.jpg",
  "image_urls": [
    "https://example.com/middle-frame-1.jpg",
    "https://example.com/middle-frame-2.jpg"
  ],
  "end_image_url": "https://example.com/end-frame.jpg",
  "prompt": "Move smoothly through the supplied frames while keeping the subject consistent.",
  "duration": 15,
  "resolution": "1080p"
}
```

## 5. Results and polling

Generation is asynchronous. A direct HTTP submission returns `request_id`, `status`, `status_url`, and `cancel_url`. Submission is not the finished video.

The SDK examples above use automatic polling. For direct HTTP integration, send authenticated GET requests to the returned `status_url`. Continue while `status` is `queued` or `in_progress`; stop on `completed`, `failed`, `nsfw`, or `canceled`. A `completed` video result exposes the generated URL as `video.url`. If generation fails, inspect the returned `error` before retrying.

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url "$STATUS_URL" \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY"
```

Set `STATUS_URL` to the URL returned by submission. Keep the same API credentials for subsequent requests.

## 6. Validation notes

Use the exact field names and values listed above. `duration` must be an integer from 3 to 30, and `resolution` must be `720p` or `1080p`. Omit unused media fields instead of sending empty strings or nulls.

The schema permits additional properties, but undocumented keys do not create new model controls. Use only the parameters documented for this endpoint.

The first frame is required even when middle or end frames are supplied. Nine or more middle frames are rejected. `aspect_ratio` is not a documented control for this mode.

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
      "image_url": "https://example.com/input.jpg",
      "resolution": "720p",
      "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
      "generate_audio": true
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
import higgsfield_client

result = higgsfield_client.subscribe(
    'lightricks/ltx-2.5/image-to-video/fast',
    arguments={'fps': 25,
         'prompt': 'A cinematic scene at sunset',
         'duration': 6,
         'image_url': 'https://example.com/input.jpg',
         'resolution': '720p',
         'aspect_ratio': '16:9',
         'generate_audio': True},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/lightricks/ltx-2.5/image-to-video/fast' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "fps": 25,
  "prompt": "A cinematic scene at sunset",
  "duration": 6,
  "image_url": "https://example.com/input.jpg",
  "resolution": "720p",
  "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
  "generate_audio": true
}
JSON
```

### Explicit lifecycle control

Use the Python SDK when a worker needs explicit status, result, or cancellation control for an existing request. The TypeScript v2 client currently exposes automatic polling through `subscribe`.

```python
import higgsfield_client

request_id = "{request_id}"
status = higgsfield_client.status(request_id=request_id)
result = higgsfield_client.result(request_id=request_id)
higgsfield_client.cancel(request_id=request_id)
```

modes.docs:
# About

**Marketing Studio Image** generates and edits campaign images. Set `enhance_prompt` to `true` to apply a Marketing Studio preset before rendering.

## 1. Direct generation or editing

Omit `image_urls` for generation. Pass one or more image URLs for editing. Direct mode is the default.

```json
{
  "prompt": "A premium skincare campaign on sculptural stone",
  "resolution": "2k",
  "aspect_ratio": "3:2",
  "enhance_prompt": false
}
```

## 2. Preset enhancement

Enhanced mode requires a preset and one product image. A second image is treated as the optional model reference. Without a second image, the composition stays product-only; the endpoint does not generate a person automatically.

### Get a preset UUID

Before sending an enhanced request, fetch the current visible presets with the same API credentials:

```http
GET https://api.higgsfield.ai/marketing-studio/image/presets?size=50
Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET
```

The endpoint returns only visible, usable Ads presets. The response contains `{ "total": ..., "cursor": ..., "items": [...] }`. Let the user select a preset, then copy the selected item's `id` into the generation request as `preset_id`:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "7e68c81e-5f97-4f48-bcab-f0d4dd75a99d",
      "type": "ads",
      "name": "Premium Product Ad"
    }
  ]
}
```

Do not hardcode preset UUIDs or source them from a static enum: presets are managed in the CMS and can change visibility. If `cursor` is not `null`, pass it to the next catalog request to load another page. The preset catalog and `preset_id` are needed only when `enhance_prompt` is `true`.

### Send the enhanced request

```json
{
  "prompt": "Minimal, bright and premium",
  "image_urls": ["https://example.com/product.png"],
  "preset_id": "7e68c81e-5f97-4f48-bcab-f0d4dd75a99d",
  "resolution": "2k",
  "aspect_ratio": "auto",
  "enhance_prompt": true
}
```

## 3. Request behavior

`resolution` supports `1k`, `2k`, and `4k`. `aspect_ratio` supports `auto`, `1:1`, `3:2`, `2:3`, `4:3`, `3:4`, `16:9`, `9:16`, and `21:9`. Enhanced requests cost 10% more than the equivalent direct request.

## 4. Authentication and queue

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/marketing-studio/image` with `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET`. The endpoint is asynchronous; poll the returned request ID or use a webhook.

# About

**MiniMax H3 Highspeed** uses the model ID `minimax/h3-highspeed/image-to-video`. Animate a first frame, a last frame or both with MiniMax H3 Highspeed. Use a prompt to guide motion and create 4–15 second videos at 480P or 768P for quick creative iteration.

## 1. Calling the API

Send requests to `https://api.higgsfield.ai/minimax/h3-highspeed/image-to-video` with a JSON body matching the parameters below.

### Install

Install an official server-side SDK. cURL needs no package.

```bash control=package group=install-typescript variant=npm label=npm when=javascript
npm install @higgsfield/client
```

```bash control=package group=install-python variant=pip label=pip when=python
pip install higgsfield-client
```

### Setup

Keep credentials in server-side environment variables. The SDKs accept the same `KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` value under their documented variable names.

```bash
export HF_CREDENTIALS="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET" # TypeScript
export HF_KEY="YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET"         # Python and cURL
```

### Request parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `string` | Yes | `—` | Prompt. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 7000. |
| `duration` | `integer` | No | `5` | Duration. Minimum: 4. Maximum: 15. |
| `image_url` | `string` | Conditional | `—` | First frame URL. Minimum length: 1. |
| `resolution` | `string` | No | `"768P"` | Resolution. Options: 480P, 768P. |
| `aspect_ratio` | `string` | No | `"auto"` | Aspect ratio. Options: auto, adaptive, 21:9, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16. |
| `end_image_url` | `string` | Conditional | `—` | Last frame URL. Minimum length: 1. |
| `aigc_watermark` | `boolean` | No | `false` |  |

## 2. Authentication

The official SDKs read credentials from the server environment and send the required `Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET` header.

### API Key

Never expose the secret in browser-side code or commit it to source control. The TypeScript SDK is server-side only. For direct HTTP calls, use:

```http
Authorization: Key $HF_KEY
```

## 3. Queue

`subscribe` submits the asynchronous request and waits for a terminal result. The TypeScript SDK polls automatically when `withPolling: true`; the Python SDK's synchronous `subscribe` call also waits. A completed request returns the generated file in the `video` field.

### Submit and wait

Replace placeholder media URLs with accessible URLs for your own files.

```ts control=language group=submit variant=javascript label=TypeScript
import { config, higgsfield } from "@higgsfield/client/v2";

config({
  credentials: process.env.HF_CREDENTIALS,
  baseURL: "https://api.higgsfield.ai",
});

const result = await higgsfield.subscribe(
  "minimax/h3-highspeed/image-to-video",
  {
    input: {
      "prompt": "Slowly move the camera toward the subject while leaves sway in the breeze",
      "duration": 5,
      "resolution": "768P",
      "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
      "image_url": "https://example.com/reference.png"
    },
    withPolling: true,
  },
);

console.log(result);
```

```python control=language group=submit variant=python label=Python
from higgsfield_client import SyncClient

client = SyncClient(base_url="https://api.higgsfield.ai")
result = client.subscribe(
    'minimax/h3-highspeed/image-to-video',
    arguments={'prompt': 'Slowly move the camera toward the subject while leaves sway in '
                   'the breeze',
         'duration': 5,
         'resolution': '768P',
         'aspect_ratio': '16:9',
         'image_url': 'https://example.com/reference.png'},
)

print(result)
```

```bash control=language group=submit variant=curl label=cURL
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.higgsfield.ai/minimax/h3-highspeed/image-to-video' \
  --header "Authorization: Key $HF_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data @- <<'JSON'
{
  "prompt": "Slowly move the camera toward the subject while leaves sway in the breeze",
  "duration": 5,
  "resolution": "768P",
  "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
  "image_url": "https://example.com/reference.png"
}
JSON
```

### Custom polling

For direct HTTP integration, submit the request and poll the returned `status_url` using the same API credentials until it reaches a terminal status. Use the returned `cancel_url` to request cancellation while the request is still queued. See the [request lifecycle guide](https://docs.higgsfield.ai/docs/concepts/requests.md) for response states.

## 4. Using this model

Provide a non-empty `prompt` of at most 7,000 characters. `duration` is an integer from 4 to 15 seconds, including every whole-second value in that range; it defaults to 5. `resolution` accepts `480P` or `768P` and defaults to `768P`.

Provide `image_url` for the first frame, `end_image_url` for the last frame, or both. At least one frame is required. Output framing adapts to the supplied keyframe.

Use the `aspect_ratio` values listed in the parameter table. Where offered, `auto` and `adaptive` derive framing from the input; text-only requests fall back to `16:9`. `aigc_watermark` is fixed to `false`.

Use URLs accessible to the service. The documentation examples use placeholder media URLs; replace them with your own image or media URL before sending a request.

## 5. Pricing

| Resolution | Output video per second |
| --- | --- |
| `480P` | $0.04 |
| `768P` | $0.06 |

The total price is output duration × the rate for the selected resolution. A 5-second video costs $0.20 at 480P or $0.30 at 768P. First and last frame images are included in that price.

| Resolution | Output video per second |

| `480P` | $0.025 |
| `768P` | $0.04 |
